name: CoreWeave
thesis: STUB: CoreWeave (CRWV) is an evaluation candidate — an AI/GPU 'neocloud' hyperscaler renting accelerated compute (NVIDIA fleets) under multi-year take-or-pay contracts. Hyper-growth, capex-heavy, and FCF-negative by design: the thesis lives or dies on contracted backlog/RPO converting to revenue faster than the debt-funded data-center buildout compounds interest + depreciation. Needs user-authored thesis + tier_1_kpis (RPO/backlog, revenue, power capacity, GPU utilization, gross margin, net leverage) + DCF params if/when it graduates to portfolio.
key_driver: Contracted RPO/backlog conversion vs. debt-funded capex compounding
thesis_breakers_qualitative: Customer concentration — a single hyperscaler/lab is a large share of revenue; non-renewal or insourcing breaks the take-or-pay base.
Net leverage / interest coverage — the buildout is debt-funded; a financing-cost spike or refinancing wall ahead of revenue ramp is the core balance-sheet risk.
GPU obsolescence / depreciation schedule — useful-life assumptions on the fleet drive both margin and the residual-value story.

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction. (FCF/OCF universals deliberately omitted: a capex-heavy, debt-funded neocloud is FCF-negative by design, so those floors would false-breach permanently — calibrate per-ticker instead.)

business_model_rules.narrative: Revenue YoY < 40% for 2Q — STUB; the neocloud hyper-growth thesis requires sustained 40%+ at current scale as contracted backlog converts. Below this, backlog conversion is stalling relative to the capex it was raised against.
Gross margin < 55% for 2Q — STUB calibration floor; sustained GPU-rental pricing erosion or under-utilization would compress GM and break the unit economics underpinning the debt-service coverage.
